# instruction.md

## Poster Brief: State of Developer Ecosystem 2024

You're creating a data-forward infographic poster (A1 portrait) that maps the shifting landscape of programming languages, databases, and cloud platforms heading into 2025. The source is a large-scale survey of **23,262 developers worldwide**, and the audience is technical — think conference hallway or tech-blog embed. They should walk away understanding one thing: **the hierarchy of programming languages is actively reshaping**, with Python closing in on JavaScript and TypeScript surging as the breakout story.

### Key Priorities

- **The language trajectory data is the centerpiece.** The 8-year arc from 2017–2024 — JavaScript's plateau at 61%, Python's climb to 57%, and TypeScript's explosive 12→37% growth — should be the most visually dominant element on the poster.
- **The "Promise Index" concept deserves a callout moment** — TypeScript at 199 signals where the ecosystem is heading, not just where it's been.
- Give the AI integration stat (18% of developers) a distinct but secondary spotlight; it's the forward-looking hook.

### Visual & Style Guidance

Lean into a **dark-mode, developer-aesthetic palette** — deep navy or charcoal backgrounds with vibrant accent colors (electric blue, amber, mint green) for data highlights. Typography should feel monospace-adjacent for headers but clean sans-serif for body text. Think IDE-inspired without being gimmicky. Charts and data visualizations should feel crisp and editorial — no 3D effects or gratuitous gradients. Use generous whitespace to let the density of data breathe.

The overall mood: **authoritative, clean, contemporary** — like a well-designed technical report, not a marketing flyer.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for all content materials (text, data, key messages).
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for poster requirements, sections, metrics, and style definitions.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final poster to `/app/output/final_poster.png`.
2. The poster must be a single self-contained image file.

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `poster.tone`, `poster.audience`, etc., use them to choose templates, palettes, and styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

# State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Wars & Rising Stars

Based on responses from **23,262 developers worldwide**, the JetBrains State of Developer Ecosystem 2024 report reveals key shifts in programming languages, databases, cloud platforms, and AI adoption.

## Top Programming Languages (2017–2024)

JavaScript remains the most-used language but its dominance is eroding, while Python and TypeScript continue their multi-year ascent.

| Language | 2017 | 2019 | 2021 | 2023 | 2024 | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | 65% | 69% | 69% | 61% | 61% | Plateau |
| Python | 32% | 49% | 52% | 54% | 57% | Steady rise |
| HTML/CSS | 60% | 61% | 60% | 52% | 51% | Gradual decline |
| SQL | 42% | 56% | 54% | 52% | 48% | Slight decline |
| Java | 47% | 50% | 49% | 49% | 46% | Gradual decline |
| TypeScript | 12% | 25% | 29% | 34% | 37% | Strong rise |
| Rust | — | 6% | 8% | 7% | 8% | All-time high |
| Go | 17% | 20% | 23% | 18% | 17% | Stable |

Python, which started at 32% in 2017 (nearly on par with PHP at 30%), is now used by more than half of the world's programmers.

## Rising Stars & the JetBrains Language Promise Index

JetBrains introduced a new **Language Promise Index** combining five-year audience growth, growth stability, intent to adopt, and user retention. The top-ranked languages signal where the ecosystem is heading.

| Rank | Language | Promise Index Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TypeScript | 199 |
| 2 | Rust | 198 |
| 3 | Python | 151 |
| 4 | Go | 129 |
| 5 | Lua | 118 |
| 6 | C++ | 113 |
| 7 | Kotlin | 113 |

Go and Rust are the languages most respondents plan to adopt, both prized for performance and concurrency. One in six Go users is considering switching to Rust. TypeScript's adoption surged from 12% in 2017 to 37% in 2024, yet JavaScript is not going anywhere — the two coexist rather than compete.

## Databases: PostgreSQL's Surge

Open-source databases dominate. PostgreSQL has seen the most dramatic growth, climbing from 32% in 2019 to 45% in 2024, narrowing the gap with long-time leader MySQL.

| Database | 2019 | 2022 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MySQL | 60% | 52% | 52% |
| PostgreSQL | 32% | 38% | 45% |
| MongoDB | 30% | 27% | 30% |
| SQLite | 29% | 27% | 30% |
| Redis | 22% | 18% | 20% |

## Cloud & Platforms: Where Code Runs

AWS leads cloud adoption at 46%, though its share has dipped from 51% in 2022. Azure (17%) and Google Cloud (11%) are slowly gaining ground.

Desktop development (53% of developers) still surpasses mobile (30%), challenging the assumption that mobile dominates. Browser platforms lead at 58%, and server/cloud infrastructure is used by 56% of developers.

## AI Integration Is Accelerating

**18% of developers** now build integrations with AI, signaling that AI is steadily infiltrating production software. Python is the dominant language for AI/ML, with 31% of Python developers involved in AI work. Notably, 11% of C++ developers also report active AI/ML involvement — a surprisingly high figure for a systems language. Fear of AI among developers appears to be diminishing year over year.

# State of Developer Ecosystem 2024: Language Wars & Rising Stars

Based on responses from **23,262 developers worldwide**, the JetBrains State of Developer Ecosystem 2024 report reveals key shifts in programming languages, databases, cloud platforms, and AI adoption.

## Top Programming Languages (2017–2024)

JavaScript remains the most-used language but its dominance is eroding, while Python and TypeScript continue their multi-year ascent.

| Language | 2017 | 2019 | 2021 | 2023 | 2024 | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | 65% | 69% | 69% | 61% | 61% | Plateau |
| Python | 32% | 49% | 52% | 54% | 57% | Steady rise |
| HTML/CSS | 60% | 61% | 60% | 52% | 51% | Gradual decline |
| SQL | 42% | 56% | 54% | 52% | 48% | Slight decline |
| Java | 47% | 50% | 49% | 49% | 46% | Gradual decline |
| TypeScript | 12% | 25% | 29% | 34% | 37% | Strong rise |
| Rust | — | 6% | 8% | 7% | 8% | All-time high |
| Go | 17% | 20% | 23% | 18% | 17% | Stable |

Python, which started at 32% in 2017 (nearly on par with PHP at 30%), is now used by more than half of the world's programmers.

## Rising Stars & the JetBrains Language Promise Index

JetBrains introduced a new **Language Promise Index** combining five-year audience growth, growth stability, intent to adopt, and user retention. The top-ranked languages signal where the ecosystem is heading.

| Rank | Language | Promise Index Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TypeScript | 199 |
| 2 | Rust | 198 |
| 3 | Python | 151 |
| 4 | Go | 129 |
| 5 | Lua | 118 |
| 6 | C++ | 113 |
| 7 | Kotlin | 113 |

Go and Rust are the languages most respondents plan to adopt, both prized for performance and concurrency. One in six Go users is considering switching to Rust. TypeScript's adoption surged from 12% in 2017 to 37% in 2024, yet JavaScript is not going anywhere — the two coexist rather than compete.

## Databases: PostgreSQL's Surge

Open-source databases dominate. PostgreSQL has seen the most dramatic growth, climbing from 32% in 2019 to 45% in 2024, narrowing the gap with long-time leader MySQL.

| Database | 2019 | 2022 | 2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| MySQL | 60% | 52% | 52% |
| PostgreSQL | 32% | 38% | 45% |
| MongoDB | 30% | 27% | 30% |
| SQLite | 29% | 27% | 30% |
| Redis | 22% | 18% | 20% |

## Cloud & Platforms: Where Code Runs

AWS leads cloud adoption at 46%, though its share has dipped from 51% in 2022. Azure (17%) and Google Cloud (11%) are slowly gaining ground.

Desktop development (53% of developers) still surpasses mobile (30%), challenging the assumption that mobile dominates. Browser platforms lead at 58%, and server/cloud infrastructure is used by 56% of developers.

## AI Integration Is Accelerating

**18% of developers** now build integrations with AI, signaling that AI is steadily infiltrating production software. Python is the dominant language for AI/ML, with 31% of Python developers involved in AI work. Notably, 11% of C++ developers also report active AI/ML involvement — a surprisingly high figure for a systems language. Fear of AI among developers appears to be diminishing year over year.

Docker adoption is strong: **49% of developers use Docker locally**, and containerization continues to be a standard part of modern development workflows.

def add_panel_border(ax, fig, color="#1e2440"):
    """Add a subtle border around a panel by drawing rectangles on the figure."""
    bbox = ax.get_position()

    w, h = bbox.width, bbox.height

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

# ── Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────
OUT = "/app/output/final_poster.png"
A1_MM = (594, 841)  # width × height mm (portrait)
DPI = 200
W_IN, H_IN = A1_MM[0] / 25.4, A1_MM[1] / 25.4
W_PX, H_PX = int(W_IN * DPI), int(H_IN * DPI)

# Palette — dark dev aesthetic
BG_DARK   = "#0b0e1a"
BG_CARD   = "#131729"
BG_CARD2  = "#181d33"
TEXT_WHITE = "#e8e8ec"
TEXT_GREY  = "#8b8fa8"
TEXT_DIM   = "#5a5e78"
BLUE      = "#4da6ff"
CYAN      = "#00d4aa"
AMBER     = "#f0a030"
ROSE      = "#f4726b"
MINT      = "#2ecc71"
PURPLE    = "#a78bfa"
ORANGE    = "#fb923c"

# ── Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
years = [2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024]
languages = {
    "JavaScript": {"vals": [65, 69, 69, 61, 61], "color": BLUE},
    "Python":     {"vals": [32, 49, 52, 54, 57], "color": CYAN},
    "HTML/CSS":   {"vals": [60, 61, 60, 52, 51], "color": TEXT_DIM},
    "SQL":        {"vals": [42, 56, 54, 52, 48], "color": "#6b7094"},
    "Java":       {"vals": [47, 50, 49, 49, 46], "color": "#7b7fa8"},
    "TypeScript": {"vals": [12, 25, 29, 34, 37], "color": AMBER},
    "Rust":       {"vals": [0,   6,  8,  7,  8], "color": ROSE},
    "Go":         {"vals": [17, 20, 23, 18, 17], "color": MINT},
}

promise_index = [
    ("TypeScript", 199, AMBER),
    ("Rust", 198, ROSE),
    ("Python", 151, CYAN),
    ("Go", 129, MINT),
    ("Lua", 118, PURPLE),
    ("C++", 113, BLUE),
    ("Kotlin", 113, ORANGE),
]

db_data = {
    "MySQL":      {"years": [2019, 2022, 2024], "vals": [60, 52, 52], "color": TEXT_DIM},
    "PostgreSQL": {"years": [2019, 2022, 2024], "vals": [32, 38, 45], "color": CYAN},
    "MongoDB":    {"years": [2019, 2022, 2024], "vals": [30, 27, 30], "color": MINT},
    "SQLite":     {"years": [2019, 2022, 2024], "vals": [29, 27, 30], "color": PURPLE},
    "Redis":      {"years": [2019, 2022, 2024], "vals": [22, 18, 20], "color": ROSE},
}

cloud = {"AWS": 46, "Azure": 17, "Google Cloud": 11}
cloud_colors = [BLUE, CYAN, AMBER]

platforms = {"Browser": 58, "Server/Cloud": 56, "Desktop": 53, "Mobile": 30}
platform_colors = [BLUE, CYAN, MINT, PURPLE]

# ── Figure Setup ────────────────────────────────────────
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W_IN, H_IN), dpi=DPI, facecolor=BG_DARK)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.06, right=0.94, top=0.96, bottom=0.03,
                    hspace=0.35, wspace=0.28)

# ── Font helpers ────────────────────────────────────────
try:
    fp_mono = FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans Mono", weight="bold")
    fp_sans = FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans")
    fp_sans_bold = FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans", weight="bold")
    fp_title = FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans Mono", weight="bold", size=28)
except Exception:
    fp_mono = FontProperties(weight="bold")
    fp_sans = FontProperties()
    fp_sans_bold = FontProperties(weight="bold")
    fp_title = FontProperties(weight="bold", size=28)

TITLE_SIZE = 26
H2_SIZE = 14
BODY_SIZE = 10
SMALL_SIZE = 8
METRIC_VALUE_SIZE = 11
METRIC_LABEL_SIZE = 7

# ── Helper: styled axes ─────────────────────────────────
def style_ax(ax, grid=True, spines=True):
    ax.set_facecolor(BG_CARD)
    if grid:
        ax.grid(True, color="#252a40", linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.7)
    if spines:
        for spine in ax.spines.values():
            spine.set_color("#252a40")
            spine.set_linewidth(0.6)
    ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_GREY, labelsize=SMALL_SIZE)
    for label in ax.get_xticklabels() + ax.get_yticklabels():
        label.set_fontproperties(fp_sans)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ROW 0 — TITLE & METRICS BAR
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
gs0 = fig.add_gridspec(1, 1, top=0.98, bottom=0.915, left=0.06, right=0.94)
ax_title = fig.add_subplot(gs0[0])
ax_title.set_facecolor(BG_DARK)
ax_title.axis("off")

# Title text
title_text = "State of Developer Ecosystem 2024"
subtitle_text = "23,262 developers surveyed  •  Language trajectories, database shifts & AI adoption heading into 2025"

fig.text(0.06, 0.975, title_text, fontproperties=fp_title, color=TEXT_WHITE, va="top",
         fontsize=TITLE_SIZE, weight="bold",
         fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono" if "DejaVu" in fp_mono.get_name() else "sans-serif")
fig.text(0.06, 0.938, subtitle_text, fontproperties=fp_sans, color=TEXT_GREY, va="top",
         fontsize=11)

# Decorative line under title
fig.text(0.06, 0.93, "━" * 118, color=BLUE, fontsize=6, va="top",
         fontfamily="monospace")

# ── Metrics bar ──
metrics = [
    ("23,262", "Survey Respondents"),
    ("61%", "JS Usage 2024"),
    ("57%", "Python Usage 2024"),
    ("12% → 37%", "TypeScript 2017→2024"),
    ("199", "Promise Index #1"),
    ("18%", "Building AI"),
    ("49%", "Use Docker"),
]
mx_start = 0.06
mx_gap = (0.94 - 0.06) / len(metrics)
for i, (val, lbl) in enumerate(metrics):
    x = mx_start + i * mx_gap + mx_gap * 0.08
    fig.text(x + mx_gap * 0.35, 0.915, val, fontproperties=fp_sans_bold, color=TEXT_WHITE,
             fontsize=METRIC_VALUE_SIZE, ha="center", va="center",
             fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
    fig.text(x + mx_gap * 0.35, 0.903, lbl, fontproperties=fp_sans, color=TEXT_GREY,
             fontsize=METRIC_LABEL_SIZE, ha="center", va="top")

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ROW 1 — LANGUAGE TRAJECTORY (centerpiece, full width)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
gs1 = fig.add_gridspec(1, 1, top=0.895, bottom=0.565, left=0.06, right=0.94)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs1[0])
style_ax(ax1)

for lang, d in languages.items():
    vals = [np.nan if v == 0 else v for v in d["vals"]]
    alpha = 0.95 if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else 0.35
    lw = 3.2 if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else 1.0
    ls = "-" if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else "--"
    ax1.plot(years, vals, color=d["color"], linewidth=lw, linestyle=ls,
             marker="o" if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else "s",
             markersize=7 if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else 3.5,
             markeredgewidth=0, alpha=alpha, zorder=5 if lang in ("JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript") else 2)

# End labels for major lines
offsets = {
    "JavaScript": (-0.08, 2),
    "Python": (-0.08, -1),
    "TypeScript": (0.05, -1),
}
for lang, d in languages.items():

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties
import numpy as np
import os

# ── Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────
OUT = "/app/output/final_poster.png"
A1_MM = (594, 841)
DPI = 200
W_IN, H_IN = A1_MM[0] / 25.4, A1_MM[1] / 25.4  # 23.386 × 33.110 inches
W_PX, H_PX = int(W_IN * DPI), int(H_IN * DPI)    # 4677 × 6622 px

# Palette
BG   = "#0b0e1a"
CARD = "#131729"
WHT  = "#e8e8ec"
GRY  = "#8b8fa8"
DIM  = "#5a5e78"
BLU  = "#4da6ff"
CYA  = "#00d4aa"
AMB  = "#f0a030"
ROS  = "#f4726b"
MNT  = "#2ecc71"
PUR  = "#a78bfa"
ORG  = "#fb923c"
GRID = "#1e2440"

# ── Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
years = [2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024]
languages = [
    ("JavaScript", [65, 69, 69, 61, 61], BLU),
    ("Python",     [32, 49, 52, 54, 57], CYA),
    ("HTML/CSS",   [60, 61, 60, 52, 51], DIM),
    ("SQL",        [42, 56, 54, 52, 48], "#6b7094"),
    ("Java",       [47, 50, 49, 49, 46], "#7b7fa8"),
    ("TypeScript", [12, 25, 29, 34, 37], AMB),
    ("Rust",       [0,   6,  8,  7,  8], ROS),
    ("Go",         [17, 20, 23, 18, 17], MNT),
]

promise = [
    ("TypeScript", 199, AMB),
    ("Rust",       198, ROS),
    ("Python",     151, CYA),
    ("Go",         129, MNT),
    ("Lua",        118, PUR),
    ("C++",        113, BLU),
    ("Kotlin",     113, ORG),
]

db_series = [
    ("MySQL",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [60, 52, 52], DIM),
    ("PostgreSQL", [2019, 2022, 2024], [32, 38, 45], CYA),
    ("MongoDB",    [2019, 2022, 2024], [30, 27, 30], MNT),
    ("SQLite",     [2019, 2022, 2024], [29, 27, 30], PUR),
    ("Redis",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [22, 18, 20], ROS),
]

cloud_data = [("AWS", 46, BLU), ("Azure", 17, CYA), ("Google Cloud", 11, AMB)]
plat_data  = [("Browser", 58, BLU), ("Server/Cloud", 56, CYA),
              ("Desktop", 53, MNT), ("Mobile", 30, PUR)]

METRICS = [
    ("23,262", "Survey\nRespondents"),
    ("61%",    "JavaScript\nUsage 2024"),
    ("57%",    "Python\nUsage 2024"),
    ("12%→37%","TypeScript\n2017 → 2024"),
    ("199",    "Promise\nIndex #1"),
    ("18%",    "Building\nAI Features"),
    ("49%",    "Use Docker\nLocally"),
]

# ── Figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W_IN, H_IN), dpi=DPI, facecolor=BG)

# ── Fonts ───────────────────────────────────────────────
def mono(size=10, bold=True):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans Mono", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)
def sans(size=10, bold=False):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)

# ── Coordinate system (fraction of full fig) ────────────
# We position everything in figure-relative coords [0,1]
# Key vertical breakpoints (from top):
Y_TOP    = 0.990   # top of title
Y_TITLE  = 0.960   # below title
Y_SUB    = 0.934   # below subtitle
Y_METRIC = 0.910   # metrics bar top
Y_METRIC_BOT = 0.876  # metrics bar bottom
Y_CHART_TOP  = 0.865   # language chart top
Y_CHART_BOT  = 0.520   # language chart bottom
Y_MID_TOP    = 0.500   # middle row top
Y_MID_BOT    = 0.280   # middle row bottom
Y_LOW_TOP    = 0.260   # lower row top
Y_LOW_BOT    = 0.090   # lower row bottom
Y_FOOTER     = 0.055   # footer
Y_BOTTOM     = 0.015   # bottom margin

X_L  = 0.060  # left margin
X_R  = 0.940  # right margin
X_M  = 0.520  # midpoint
X_M2 = 0.660  # 2/3 point

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TITLE SECTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.text(X_L, Y_TOP, "▌", fontsize=18, color=BLU, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")
fig.text(X_L + 0.014, Y_TOP, "State of Developer Ecosystem 2024",
         fontsize=28, color=WHT, va="top", fontweight="bold",
         fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
fig.text(X_L + 0.014, Y_SUB,
         "23,262 developers surveyed worldwide  •  Language trajectories, database shifts & AI adoption heading into 2025",
         fontsize=10, color=GRY, va="top", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")
fig.text(X_L, Y_SUB - 0.012, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=BLU, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# METRICS BAR
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_metrics = len(METRICS)
slot_w = (X_R - X_L) / n_metrics
for i, (val, lbl) in enumerate(METRICS):
    cx = X_L + slot_w * i + slot_w / 2
    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC, val, fontsize=12, color=WHT, ha="center", va="center",
             fontweight="bold", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC - 0.015, lbl, fontsize=6.5, color=GRY, ha="center", va="top",
             fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")

# Divider line
fig.text(X_L, Y_METRIC_BOT, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=GRID, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CHART 1: Language Trajectories (full width, large)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ax_lang = fig.add_axes([X_L, Y_CHART_BOT, X_R - X_L, Y_CHART_TOP - Y_CHART_BOT])
ax_lang.set_facecolor(CARD)
ax_lang.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.6)
for spine in ax_lang.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(GRID); spine.set_linewidth(0.5)

# Plot lines
highlight = {"JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript"}
for name, vals, color in languages:
    v = [np.nan if x == 0 else x for x in vals]
    major = name in highlight
    ax_lang.plot(years, v, color=color, linewidth=3.5 if major else 1.2,
                 linestyle="-" if major else "--",
                 marker="o" if major else "s",
                 markersize=8 if major else 3, markeredgewidth=0,
                 alpha=0.95 if major else 0.35,
                 zorder=5 if major else 2)

# End labels for major languages
label_data = [
    ("JavaScript", 61, (-0.10, 2.5)),
    ("Python",     57, (-0.10, -1.5)),
    ("TypeScript", 37, (0.08, 0)),
]
for name, val, (dx, dy) in label_data:
    ax_lang.annotate(f"{name}  {val}%", xy=(2024, val),
                     xytext=(2024 + dx, val + dy), fontsize=11,
                     color={"JavaScript": BLU, "Python": CYA, "TypeScript": AMB}[name],
                     fontweight="bold", va="center", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")

# Minor language labels in a sidebar
minor_y = 0.92
for name, vals, color in languages:
    if name not in highlight:

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties
import numpy as np
import os

# ── Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────
OUT = "/app/output/final_poster.png"
A1_MM = (594, 841)
DPI = 200
W_IN, H_IN = A1_MM[0] / 25.4, A1_MM[1] / 25.4  # 23.386 × 33.110 inches
W_PX, H_PX = int(W_IN * DPI), int(H_IN * DPI)    # 4677 × 6622 px

# Palette
BG   = "#0b0e1a"
CARD = "#131729"
WHT  = "#e8e8ec"
GRY  = "#8b8fa8"
DIM  = "#5a5e78"
BLU  = "#4da6ff"
CYA  = "#00d4aa"
AMB  = "#f0a030"
ROS  = "#f4726b"
MNT  = "#2ecc71"
PUR  = "#a78bfa"
ORG  = "#fb923c"
GRID = "#1e2440"

# ── Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
years = [2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024]
languages = [
    ("JavaScript", [65, 69, 69, 61, 61], BLU),
    ("Python",     [32, 49, 52, 54, 57], CYA),
    ("HTML/CSS",   [60, 61, 60, 52, 51], DIM),
    ("SQL",        [42, 56, 54, 52, 48], "#6b7094"),
    ("Java",       [47, 50, 49, 49, 46], "#7b7fa8"),
    ("TypeScript", [12, 25, 29, 34, 37], AMB),
    ("Rust",       [0,   6,  8,  7,  8], ROS),
    ("Go",         [17, 20, 23, 18, 17], MNT),
]

promise = [
    ("TypeScript", 199, AMB),
    ("Rust",       198, ROS),
    ("Python",     151, CYA),
    ("Go",         129, MNT),
    ("Lua",        118, PUR),
    ("C++",        113, BLU),
    ("Kotlin",     113, ORG),
]

db_series = [
    ("MySQL",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [60, 52, 52], DIM),
    ("PostgreSQL", [2019, 2022, 2024], [32, 38, 45], CYA),
    ("MongoDB",    [2019, 2022, 2024], [30, 27, 30], MNT),
    ("SQLite",     [2019, 2022, 2024], [29, 27, 30], PUR),
    ("Redis",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [22, 18, 20], ROS),
]

cloud_data = [("AWS", 46, BLU), ("Azure", 17, CYA), ("Google Cloud", 11, AMB)]
plat_data  = [("Browser", 58, BLU), ("Server/Cloud", 56, CYA),
              ("Desktop", 53, MNT), ("Mobile", 30, PUR)]

METRICS = [
    ("23,262", "Survey\nRespondents"),
    ("61%",    "JavaScript\nUsage 2024"),
    ("57%",    "Python\nUsage 2024"),
    ("12%→37%","TypeScript\n2017 → 2024"),
    ("199",    "Promise\nIndex #1"),
    ("18%",    "Building\nAI Features"),
    ("49%",    "Use Docker\nLocally"),
]

def mono(size=10, bold=True):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans Mono", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)
def sans(size=10, bold=False):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)

# ── Coordinate system (fraction of full fig) ────────────
# We position everything in figure-relative coords [0,1]
# Key vertical breakpoints (from top):
Y_TOP    = 0.990   # top of title
Y_TITLE  = 0.960   # below title
Y_SUB    = 0.934   # below subtitle
Y_METRIC = 0.910   # metrics bar top
Y_METRIC_BOT = 0.876  # metrics bar bottom
Y_CHART_TOP  = 0.865   # language chart top
Y_CHART_BOT  = 0.520   # language chart bottom
Y_MID_TOP    = 0.500   # middle row top
Y_MID_BOT    = 0.280   # middle row bottom
Y_LOW_TOP    = 0.260   # lower row top
Y_LOW_BOT    = 0.090   # lower row bottom
Y_FOOTER     = 0.055   # footer
Y_BOTTOM     = 0.015   # bottom margin

X_L  = 0.060  # left margin
X_R  = 0.940  # right margin
X_M  = 0.520  # midpoint
X_M2 = 0.660  # 2/3 point

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

         fontsize=28, color=WHT, va="top", fontweight="bold",
         fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
fig.text(X_L + 0.014, Y_SUB,
         "23,262 developers surveyed worldwide  •  Language trajectories, database shifts & AI adoption heading into 2025",
         fontsize=10, color=GRY, va="top", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")
fig.text(X_L, Y_SUB - 0.012, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=BLU, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# METRICS BAR
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_metrics = len(METRICS)
slot_w = (X_R - X_L) / n_metrics
for i, (val, lbl) in enumerate(METRICS):
    cx = X_L + slot_w * i + slot_w / 2
    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC, val, fontsize=12, color=WHT, ha="center", va="center",

    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC - 0.015, lbl, fontsize=6.5, color=GRY, ha="center", va="top",
             fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")

# Divider line
fig.text(X_L, Y_METRIC_BOT, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=GRID, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

for spine in ax_lang.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(GRID); spine.set_linewidth(0.5)

# Plot lines
highlight = {"JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript"}
for name, vals, color in languages:

                 zorder=5 if major else 2)

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.font_manager import FontProperties
import numpy as np
import os

# ── Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────
OUT = "/app/output/final_poster.png"
A1_MM = (594, 841)
DPI = 200
W_IN, H_IN = A1_MM[0] / 25.4, A1_MM[1] / 25.4  # 23.386 × 33.110 inches
W_PX, H_PX = int(W_IN * DPI), int(H_IN * DPI)    # 4677 × 6622 px

# Palette
BG   = "#0b0e1a"
CARD = "#131729"
WHT  = "#e8e8ec"
GRY  = "#8b8fa8"
DIM  = "#5a5e78"
BLU  = "#4da6ff"
CYA  = "#00d4aa"
AMB  = "#f0a030"
ROS  = "#f4726b"
MNT  = "#2ecc71"
PUR  = "#a78bfa"
ORG  = "#fb923c"
GRID = "#1e2440"

# ── Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────
years = [2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024]
languages = [
    ("JavaScript", [65, 69, 69, 61, 61], BLU),
    ("Python",     [32, 49, 52, 54, 57], CYA),
    ("HTML/CSS",   [60, 61, 60, 52, 51], DIM),
    ("SQL",        [42, 56, 54, 52, 48], "#6b7094"),
    ("Java",       [47, 50, 49, 49, 46], "#7b7fa8"),
    ("TypeScript", [12, 25, 29, 34, 37], AMB),
    ("Rust",       [0,   6,  8,  7,  8], ROS),
    ("Go",         [17, 20, 23, 18, 17], MNT),
]

promise = [
    ("TypeScript", 199, AMB),
    ("Rust",       198, ROS),
    ("Python",     151, CYA),
    ("Go",         129, MNT),
    ("Lua",        118, PUR),
    ("C++",        113, BLU),
    ("Kotlin",     113, ORG),
]

db_series = [
    ("MySQL",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [60, 52, 52], DIM),
    ("PostgreSQL", [2019, 2022, 2024], [32, 38, 45], CYA),
    ("MongoDB",    [2019, 2022, 2024], [30, 27, 30], MNT),
    ("SQLite",     [2019, 2022, 2024], [29, 27, 30], PUR),
    ("Redis",      [2019, 2022, 2024], [22, 18, 20], ROS),
]

cloud_data = [("AWS", 46, BLU), ("Azure", 17, CYA), ("Google Cloud", 11, AMB)]
plat_data  = [("Browser", 58, BLU), ("Server/Cloud", 56, CYA),
              ("Desktop", 53, MNT), ("Mobile", 30, PUR)]

METRICS = [
    ("23,262", "Survey\nRespondents"),
    ("61%",    "JavaScript\nUsage 2024"),
    ("57%",    "Python\nUsage 2024"),
    ("12%→37%","TypeScript\n2017 → 2024"),
    ("199",    "Promise\nIndex #1"),
    ("18%",    "Building\nAI Features"),
    ("49%",    "Use Docker\nLocally"),
]

# ── Figure ──────────────────────────────────────────────
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(W_IN, H_IN), dpi=DPI, facecolor=BG)

# ── Fonts ───────────────────────────────────────────────
def mono(size=10, bold=True):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans Mono", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)
def sans(size=10, bold=False):
    return FontProperties(family="DejaVu Sans", weight="bold" if bold else "normal", size=size)

# ── Coordinate system (fraction of full fig) ────────────
# We position everything in figure-relative coords [0,1]
# Key vertical breakpoints (from top):
Y_TOP    = 0.990   # top of title
Y_TITLE  = 0.960   # below title
Y_SUB    = 0.934   # below subtitle
Y_METRIC = 0.910   # metrics bar top
Y_METRIC_BOT = 0.876  # metrics bar bottom
Y_CHART_TOP  = 0.865   # language chart top
Y_CHART_BOT  = 0.520   # language chart bottom
Y_MID_TOP    = 0.500   # middle row top
Y_MID_BOT    = 0.280   # middle row bottom
Y_LOW_TOP    = 0.260   # lower row top
Y_LOW_BOT    = 0.090   # lower row bottom
Y_FOOTER     = 0.055   # footer
Y_BOTTOM     = 0.015   # bottom margin

X_L  = 0.060  # left margin
X_R  = 0.940  # right margin
X_M  = 0.520  # midpoint
X_M2 = 0.660  # 2/3 point

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TITLE SECTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig.text(X_L, Y_TOP, "▌", fontsize=18, color=BLU, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")
fig.text(X_L + 0.014, Y_TOP, "State of Developer Ecosystem 2024",
         fontsize=28, color=WHT, va="top", fontweight="bold",
         fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
fig.text(X_L + 0.014, Y_SUB,
         "23,262 developers surveyed worldwide  •  Language trajectories, database shifts & AI adoption heading into 2025",
         fontsize=10, color=GRY, va="top", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")
fig.text(X_L, Y_SUB - 0.012, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=BLU, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# METRICS BAR
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_metrics = len(METRICS)
slot_w = (X_R - X_L) / n_metrics
for i, (val, lbl) in enumerate(METRICS):
    cx = X_L + slot_w * i + slot_w / 2
    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC, val, fontsize=12, color=WHT, ha="center", va="center",
             fontweight="bold", fontfamily="DejaVu Sans Mono")
    fig.text(cx, Y_METRIC - 0.015, lbl, fontsize=6.5, color=GRY, ha="center", va="top",
             fontfamily="DejaVu Sans")

# Divider line
fig.text(X_L, Y_METRIC_BOT, "━" * 125, fontsize=5, color=GRID, va="top", fontfamily="monospace")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CHART 1: Language Trajectories (full width, large)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ax_lang = fig.add_axes([X_L, Y_CHART_BOT, X_R - X_L, Y_CHART_TOP - Y_CHART_BOT])
ax_lang.set_facecolor(CARD)
ax_lang.grid(True, color=GRID, linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.6)
for spine in ax_lang.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(GRID); spine.set_linewidth(0.5)

# Plot lines
highlight = {"JavaScript", "Python", "TypeScript"}
for name, vals, color in languages:
    v = [np.nan if x == 0 else x for x in vals]
    major = name in highlight
    ax_lang.plot(years, v, color=color, linewidth=3.5 if major else 1.2,
